title: Maximum Value after Insertion
summary: Given a large integer n as a string and an integer digit x, insert x into n to maximize its value.
statement: Given a large integer n as a string and an integer digit x, insert x into n to maximize its value. Do not place x before the negative sign if n is negative. For instance, inserting 6 into 73 results in 763, and inserting 2 into -55 results in -255.
constraints: n represents a nonzero integer using 1 through 100000 characters.
Its digits and x are in 1 through 9.
Insert x exactly once and never before a leading minus sign.
hints: For a positive number, place x before the first smaller digit.
For a negative number, maximize the value by minimizing magnitude: place x before the first larger digit.
If no improving position exists, append x at the end.
All earlier digits stay equal between candidates, so the first differing digit determines the larger integer and validates the greedy stopping point.
editorial: All earlier digits stay equal between candidates, so the first differing digit determines the larger integer and validates the greedy stopping point.

tests.explanation: Every insertion produces the same maximal representation, 999.
Inserting two before three gives -123, which is greater than -213 or -132.
